name: Kamat Hotels (India) Ltd
title: Kamat Hotels (India) Ltd - 526668 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Hotel operator (asset-light, leased) reports Q1 FY27 revenue up 10% to Rs 91 cr and EBITDA up 36% to Rs 25 cr; no supply discipline data, capex limited, pipeline ~400 keys in 12-15 months.

capex.quote: most of our properties are on lease where our component of CAPEX is very minimum

triggers.label: RevPAR growth ~18% Orchid, 17% Lotus
triggers.quote: RevPAR for our two brands that is Orchid and Lotus grew 18% and 17% respectively in Q1 FY27

triggers.label: Orchid ARR flat, growth via occupancy
triggers.quote: we decided to keep rates flat and sell more and more rooms

triggers.label: ~400 keys added in 12-15 months
triggers.quote: we are looking at around 400 keys addition, maybe next one year or 15 months from now

summary.headline: Kamat Hotels Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to INR 91 crore and EBITDA 36% to INR 25 crore, margin 27% vs 22%.

financial_highlights.change: +10% YoY vs INR 83 crore in Q1 FY26
+36% YoY vs INR 18 crore in Q1 FY26
Achieved despite four new properties added

financial_highlights.metric: Same-store revenue (excl. Ira Mumbai and four new hotels)

financial_highlights.value: Revenue up 35% YoY; EBITDA up 50% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Ira by Orchid (excl. Ira Mumbai) ARR / RevPAR
financial_highlights.value: ARR about INR 4,069 (flattish); RevPAR about INR 2,466 (about 3% growth)

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated debt / cash and FDs / net debt (as of last quarter)
financial_highlights.value: Debt INR 105 crore; cash and FDs INR 65 crore; net debt INR 38 crore

segments.name: Orchid Mumbai (business hotel)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 35% YoY and EBITDA up 50% YoY; occupancy reached about 91% with RevPAR up almost 40%, rates kept flat to sell more rooms.

segments.name: Orchid Pune (business hotel)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 27% YoY; management is rationalising costs to improve margins and sees upgrade potential to upper upscale.

segments.name: Ira by Orchid portfolio
segments.commentary: Reported negative RevPAR growth including Ira Mumbai, which closed on 31 March 2026; excluding Ira Mumbai, ARR about INR 4,069 and RevPAR about INR 2,466 (about 3% growth). Ira by Orchid Hyderabad is ramping up after a weak FY26.

segments.name: Newer leased properties (Orchid Panchgani, Orchid Rishikesh/Rishivan, Ira Hyderabad, Ira Bhavnagar)
segments.commentary: Four new hotels added in the last 2-3 quarters are still scaling up and carry higher operating costs. Management said Bhavnagar opened recently with strong banqueting response and will be in its full-year base next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are the properties due to open this quarter on schedule, or have LPG, construction or supply shortages delayed them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no supply-chain impact from the war; Dwarka is due November-December, Gwalior around October-November, and Dehradun may slip about six months due to owner challenges.

qa_highlights.question: What occupancy trajectory is expected for Q2 and Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the Q1 occupancy growth trend to continue for the remaining three quarters, with business hotels typically above 75-80% and leisure properties seasonal.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a strategic pivot under the new CFO, and will the company move towards owned hotels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is evaluating various growth options and will combine asset-light leases or revenue share with owned hotels (brownfield or land parcels); debt capacity up to INR 300 crore at three times forward EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Are any hotels opened before FY26 loss-making, and what is the plan for loss-makers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hotels opened in FY24-FY25 are all profitable after lease charges; new hotels usually show losses in year one due to opening costs and take two to three years to stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company take price hikes given flat Orchid ARR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RevPAR is the key metric and that rates and occupancy are managed case by case depending on micro-market demand and competition.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA margin improvement, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the margin improvement long-term, with a 30% target in two to three years through revenue growth and cost control, including renewable energy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline and expected room additions in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 400 keys over the next 12-15 months across Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi, with possible delays.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for FY27 and FY28, and what was spent in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Most properties are leased, so capex is minimal; Mumbai and Pune renovation plans are being finalised, with guidance expected next quarter, and only normal repair and maintenance capex is planned for the next two years.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance for FY27 top line or EBITDA; management said it expects sequential (QoQ) growth in the coming quarters, supported by tailwinds.
Occupancy expected to keep its Q1 growth trend over the remaining three quarters; business hotels typically cross 75-80% occupancy and leisure properties are seasonal.
EBITDA margin target of 30%, to be reached in about two to three years, through higher revenue and cost control including renewable energy for some properties.
About 400 keys expected to be added in the next 12-15 months: Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi (Kutch), with possible delays.
Net debt to move towards zero; management said debt capacity of up to INR 300 crore exists at three times forward EBITDA.

Renovation/refurbishment capex for Mumbai and Pune hotels is being designed; guidance on it expected next quarter. Non-lease capex for new projects is not yet on the books, with only normal repair and maintenance capex for the next two years.
capex_capacity: Opening timelines: Orchid Dwarka (63 rooms) targeted for November-December 2026; Gwalior targeted for around October-November 2026 (Diwali); Nashik targeted before the Kumbh; Dehradun may slip by about six months due to owner-side challenges; Rishikesh expansion and Mandvi are on track.
Most properties are on lease, so the company's capex component is minimal; renovation of Mumbai and Pune hotels is planned, with design being finalised.

No new owned or brownfield project is currently on the books; any future project would add capex. Management is evaluating both asset-light (lease or revenue share) and owned hotels, including brownfield refurbishments and land parcels in deep markets.
Ira Mumbai lease ended on 31 March 2026; the company said it is not adding hotels in Mumbai or Pune and is focusing on new cities where it has no presence.
demand_pricing: Occupancy up in Q1 FY27 on domestic business and leisure tailwinds; reduced outbound travel by Indians to the Middle East and Southeast Asia due to the war and fuel shortages cited as a driver.
RevPAR growth of 18% (Orchid) and 17% (Lotus) in Q1 FY27, which management called well above the industry.
Pricing approach is case by case: in Mumbai, rates were held flat to drive occupancy; in Pune, both rate and occupancy are being pushed; management said there is no thumb rule.
Industry context per management: domestic tourism CAGR of about 10-12% over the next 3-4 years; Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities expected to contribute over 60% of new branded hotel supply.
Bhavnagar demand supported by Dholera industrial activity, new flights (including Navi Mumbai-Bhavnagar) and NRI and wedding demand in the post-monsoon season.
risks_watch: Owner-driven delays: Dehradun may slip about six months and Nashik has technical delays, affecting the 400-key addition plan.
Ramp-up drag from four new hotels and first-year opening losses, with Ira Hyderabad and Bhavnagar still stabilising; Ira Mumbai closure lowers the Ira portfolio base.
Flat ARR at Orchid and Ira by Orchid (ARR about INR 4,069, flattish) against heavy reliance on occupancy-led RevPAR growth, which may face competitive resistance.
Part of the tailwind came from reduced outbound travel due to the war and fuel shortages, which may not persist.
Capital allocation is undecided: management is evaluating growth options, and the mix between leases and owned hotels and the Mumbai/Pune renovation capex are yet to be guided.
Watch in Q2: whether Orchid Dwarka and Gwalior open on schedule, the renovation capex guidance, and sequential revenue and EBITDA growth.
key_quotes: Driven by again efficiency and I must appreciate our team for their pricing discipline and their operational efficiency, which translated into a phenomenal improvement in our EBITDA rising to 36% high, Rs. 25 crores from the previous quarter in the same year.
So, we are evaluating various growth options. I mean, I don't want to say anything now.
So, we don't want to give any guidance as such. But what we can tell you is the tailwinds or growth drivers are very strong, and we are expected to show growth on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
Pranav, this is long-term. I mean, our target is to take EBITDA margins up to 30% and it comes from both.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q1 numbers and the demand backdrop, but guarded on forward specifics: management repeatedly declined to give numerical guidance and to discuss unsigned projects. Candid on owner-driven delays (Dehradun, Nashik) and on the first-year losses of new hotels.

adds.what: Nashik hotel opening before the Kumbh
Dehradun hotel, may slip about six months
Rishikesh expansion and Mandvi (Kutch) hotel, on track; about 400 keys added in 12-15 months across all six

growth.why: No numerical FY27 guidance, but management expects sequential growth, Q1 revenue rose 10% with same-store revenue up 17%, and about 400 keys are being added over 12-15 months; the capacity is mostly leased with minimal capex, and ramp-up of the four new hotels is still pending.
